svg.text: Repository-grounded view of the implemented Qt/C++ system, annotated against the COS202 lab-manual requirements

g.text: Owns/deletes patient objects; cache is non-owning.
Concrete pages and handlers are implemented here.
Search/report pages are not separate classes.
Does not own the shared manager (main.cpp).
Separate compiled panel class; MainWindow builds its own view.
− patient selector / date / time / reason / table
Separate compiled panel class; not instantiated by MainWindow.
Validates input; generates IDs; delegates storage.
Uses IDGenerator and may throw ClinicException.
Owns database and queue/stack containers; queued patient
pointers refer to database objects (not queue-owned).
struct · stored by value in undoStack
Snapshot pointer is owned/deleted by manager until restored.
Used by AppointmentController; sequence is atomic.
caught and shown by GUI panels.
The header is empty and persistence is not implemented or wired into the running application.
MainWindow declares New / Save / Load handlers, but this diagram does not imply file persistence.
main.cpp creates one ClinicManager and passes it by reference to MainWindow.

svg.text: Runtime polymorphism: ClinicDatabase stores PatientRecord* to the three concrete subclasses; virtual getPatientType() / displayDetails() are overridden.
The lab manual requests an abstract Appointable interface, but this repository does not implement one: model/Appointable.h instead contains a duplicate Model::Appointment definition and is not built.
The patient–appointment link is currently the appointment's patientID string; appointments are not stored inside individual PatientRecord objects. File persistence is also absent.
Solid diamond = ownership/composition; open triangle = inheritance; hollow arrow = directed association; dashed arrow = dependency. Multiplicities are shown where the stored relationship is explicit.
